label: comment-contradicts-adjacent-code
name: A comment, log label, doc clause or notation disagrees with the code it sits on, or reads two ways
description: What breaks: a comment names flag prep_done while the loop waits on hw_prepared (3307483528 'you mean hw_prepared?'); a header comment says the FUSE path uses <bdf> while code uses dev->idx (3405930260 'I suspect this got copied from other (inaccurate) fuse-related comments'); a comment says hbm_cnt comes from ares_fields while line 1138 reads wres_fields (3437533506); a Note says compute_forward_args 'performs' a recursion the PR removed (3120684367); a comment still asks a design question the same PR answers (2789661703); a log label says HW O while the value printed is Ra (2771718489 'We don't have an O until we divide Ra by SUME, right?'); two log lines share one format text for K and V (3002066935); Q.61 next to '3 integer bits' (3356922988); '(no shuffle)' where the input is pre-shuffled (2828677364); a comment cites a file path that exists only on the author's machine (3227565141); '(C2C egress excepted)' reads two ways (4095187050); a trailing comment restates the identifier (3002013791). Procedure: for every added comment, log or doc sentence extract each identifier, path, number, tense verb and negation; verify each against the code lines it describes and the file system; expand every elided clause into one full sentence. Mostly suggestion blocks with the corrected line plus '... right?'. Offer both repairs (fix the code or fix the text).
disposition_reason: Check 6 covers compile-time guarantee sentences only; identifier-by-identifier comparison of a comment with the lines below it is a different procedure. 12 rows over 11 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes: identifier and path comparison is mechanical; the hardware meaning of Ra vs O (2771718489) and the notation (3356922988) need domain knowledge.

members.concern: A new code comment inside the dma_xfer_state struct (the DMA transfer completion record) still asks 'What are the done conditions for this xfer?', a question this very PR answers, so the comment reads as stale thinking left in the code.

detection.trigger: An added comment line in a header or source hunk is phrased as an open question or a design-time musing ('What are ...?', 'we had originally thought', 'proposed change', 'TODO: decide') about behaviour that the same PR implements.
detection.procedure: Grep the diff's added comment lines for '?' and for 'originally', 'proposed', 'we should', 'later'. For each hit read the surrounding struct or function at HEAD and check whether the fields or code below the comment already settle the question. Also check whether the same PR removes a sibling comment that the question referred to (here driver.cpp removed the 'Proposed change to how we detect doneness' block).
detection.question: Does the code at HEAD already answer the question the comment asks, so that a reader gains nothing from it?

members.quote: this question/comment doesn't seem relevant... you're answering it with this work right?
members.note: At head d4795f37a5 the line 'What are the done conditions for this xfer?' is gone; the struct now documents end_desc/end_wrap_count/readback fields with default member initializers (device.hpp lines 179-201, read with git show). The author agreed the comment did not say what he intended.

members.concern: The new comment above the TX wait says the PREP thread 'has almost certainly already set prep_done', but the loop below waits on hw_prepared (the other wqentry flag); Wade asks whether the comment means hw_prepared.

detection.trigger: An added comment names a flag, variable or function, and the code lines directly below it read or write a different identifier of the same family (two atomics declared side by side in the same struct).
detection.procedure: For each added comment that names an identifier, take the next non-comment statements and list the identifiers they use; if the comment's identifier is not among them but a sibling (same declaring struct, h/pos/device.hpp prep_done / hw_prepared) is, report the mismatch and ask which one is meant.
detection.question: Does the identifier the comment names match the identifier the code under it actually checks?

members.quote:
"... almost certainly already set prep_done"

you mean 'hw_prepared'?
members.note: Wade knew the two flags are distinct (h/pos/device.hpp declares both atomics: prep_done{1} at :107, hw_prepared{0} at :110). Head worker.cpp:1062 reads 'already set hw_prepared.' (fixed); the dbg_tx_log at :1070 still says 'done waiting for prep_done' (a second instance Wade did not flag).

members.concern: The header comment says the FUSE stats path uses <bdf> (the PCI bus:device.function address) but the code registers the path with dev->idx (the device index), so the comment is wrong; Wade supplies the corrected line and guesses it was copied from other inaccurate comments.

detection.trigger: a diff adds a comment that states a concrete runtime string, path, name or number (a FUSE path, a file name, a count) next to a declaration
detection.procedure: for each such comment, find the definition (grep src/ for the function name; here src/pos/device.cpp:625-630 builds fmt::format("/rinzler/stats/devices/{}/wcmd_reuse/{}", dev->idx, e.leaf)) and compare each placeholder in the comment with the variable actually formatted; also grep h/ for the same comment text to see whether it was copied from a sibling declaration
detection.question: Does the literal path or name in the comment match what the implementation actually produces, placeholder by placeholder?

members.quote: ... right? You're using dev->idx, not bdf. I suspect this got copied from other (inaccurate) fuse-related comments.
members.note: Verified: at 247c8a4c22 src/pos/device.cpp:625 and :630 format the path with dev->idx. The sibling comment for pos_devices_register_fuse_stats in h/pos/alloc.hpp:226 also says <bdf>, which is the copy source Wade suspected. Final head device.hpp:663 reads <idx>. Wade used a GitHub suggestion block with the exact replacement line.

members.concern: The new Note comment says compute_forward_args 'performs' a recursive depth-first search in the present tense, but the PR removes the recursion, so the sentence should be past tense.

detection.trigger: A comment hunk describes, in the present tense, a behavior that the same diff removes or replaces (recursion, an old algorithm, an old data structure).
detection.procedure: For each added or kept comment line near a changed function, list the mechanism nouns and verbs it uses (recursive, stack frame, lookup table). Grep the function body at HEAD for the mechanism; if the diff removed it, the sentence must be past tense or rewritten.
detection.question: Does the code at HEAD still do what this comment sentence says it does, in the tense the sentence uses?

members.note: Verified at head 269418ce4d line 1328: the text reads 'performed'. Commit 6 'Apply suggestion from @Wado-posi'. Wade changed one word: performs -> performed.

members.concern: The header comment of prepare_and_stage_legacy says hbm_cnt is captured from ares_fields (the activation command word) but the code at line 1138 captures it from wres_fields (the weights command word); Wade suggests the comment name be corrected.

detection.trigger: A comment added or kept in the diff names a code identifier (variable, field, function) in a claim about what the code does ('X is captured from Y').
detection.procedure: For every identifier inside an added or surviving comment, grep the function body below for the statement the comment describes and compare the identifier used (here 'hbm_cnt = wres_fields.fields.hbm_cnt;' at :1138 vs the comment's 'ares_fields'). Also verify the named identifier exists in scope: ares_fields is the activation word in prepare_cmd_words, wres_fields the weights word.
detection.question: Does the code statement the comment describes use the identifier the comment names?

members.quote:
```suggestion
// hbm_cnt is captured from wres_fields before any WLR mutation; it is needed
```

per line 1138 below
members.note: Verified at c68ea87f48 worker.cpp:1138 'hbm_cnt = wres_fields.fields.hbm_cnt;'. Applied at head :1112 comment reads 'wres_fields'. Wade cites the code line as the evidence ('per line 1138 below'): comment-vs-code mismatch with the deciding line named. Both ares_fields (activation cmd, :553-716) and wres_fields exist in the file, so the wrong name is plausible-looking and only reading the body catches it.

members.concern: The debug log line still labels the printed value `HW O` (the normalized attention output), but the variable now printed is `hw_Ra_val`, the un-normalized accumulator Ra, which only becomes O after division by SUME (the softmax denominator); Wade asks why the label was not updated.

detection.trigger: A hunk renames or re-derives a variable (here `hw_O_val` -> `hw_Ra_val`, dropping the `/ *hw_sume` division) while a format string, log label, comment or identifier in the same or an adjacent unchanged line keeps the old name or the old quantity.
detection.procedure: For each renamed or re-derived variable in the diff, list the string literals, comments and identifiers within the same statement block that mention the old name or old quantity (grep the old stem, e.g. `O`, `HW O`, in the lines around the hunk at HEAD). Check whether the semantic relation stated by the old label still holds for the new value (here O = Ra / SUME, so Ra is not O).
detection.question: Does every label, format string and comment next to the changed variable describe the quantity that is now computed, not the one computed before the change?

members.quote: why are you calling this `HW O` if you're printing the Ra value? We don't have an `O` until we divide Ra by SUME, right?
members.note: The fact Wade relied on is visible in the hunk: the removed line `float hw_O_val = (static_cast<float>(hw_head[i])) / *hw_sume;` divided by SUME, the added line `float hw_Ra_val = (static_cast<float>(hw_head[i]));` does not, and the format string on the next line still says 'HW O:'. Verified at c502e4d61a:644 the string reads 'HW Ra:'. Commit subject in this PR: 'shift to checking vs Ra and not O. v_stars are NOT scaled values.' Check 5 covers a test name contradicting assertions; the same theme (a label says one thing, the code does another) but the trigger as written (TEST_CASE/SECTION name) does not fire on a log string in production debug code.

members.concern: Two consecutive debug log lines (one for the K weight command, one for V) use the identical format text 'wcmd_vals[{}]', so the K line should say which command it is; he suggests 'kcmd_vals[{}]'.

detection.trigger: A diff adds two or more log/format calls with identical format strings whose arguments differ (kwcmd vs vwcmd), or a format string naming a variable other than the one passed.
detection.procedure: For each added log call, compare the format string with the argument list and with adjacent log calls; flag identical strings fed with different objects.
detection.question: Can a reader of the log output tell the two lines apart?

members.note: Head af9438799a src/pos/worker.cpp ~988-997: both dbg_hwattn_cmds_log calls still say 'wcmd_vals[{}]'; the first logs kwcmd at w_idx-2, the second vwcmd at w_idx-1. Not applied. Note the suggested name 'kcmd_vals' is not a real array (the array is wcmd_vals); the suggestion is about the label, not the identifier.

members.concern: Asks whether the fixed-point format in the new Note [Cycle Frequency Reciprocals] should be written Q3.61 (3 integer bits, 61 fractional bits) instead of Q.61, since the comment itself says 3 integer bits are reserved.

detection.trigger: a comment or Note introduces a standard notation (fixed-point Qm.n, SI units, IEEE format names, big-O) and the symbol it writes contradicts a fact stated in the same comment (e.g. 'Q.61' next to '3 integer bits')
detection.procedure: read every added comment block in the diff; for each notation token (regex `Q\.?\d+`, `Q\d+\.\d+`), compare the integer-bit count it implies with the integer-bit count the surrounding sentences state; also compare with identifier suffixes (`_q61`) and assert messages that spell the same format
detection.question: does the notation as written mean what the surrounding comment says it means?

members.quote: I think technically this should be `Q3.61` right? Not `Q.61`?
members.note: Hunk text: 'Both reciprocals are Q.61: 3 integer bits handle the integer part' - the contradiction is inside the added comment. Author fixed in 34d878186 (commit subject 'Use standard Q3.61 notation in comments') and kept the `_q61` variable suffix, with the Note now stating the suffix names only the fractional-bit count. Wade approved in the same minute at the same commit 47df863d13, so the nit did not gate approval.

members.concern: Wade suggests the new comment line 'These functions transfer pre-constructed cacheblocks (no shuffle) to HBM' would read better as 'pre-shuffled cacheblocks', because the input blocks have already been shuffled; '(no shuffle)' can be read as 'unshuffled' (HBM = the FPGA's high-bandwidth memory; shuffle = the layout transform that builds a cacheblock).

detection.trigger: A comment hunk describes a function with a negated parenthetical ('(no X)', 'without X', 'skips X') where X is a step that happens elsewhere on the same data before the call.
detection.procedure: Read the function the comment describes and the usage example in the same comment block (here '// ... populate k_block via shuffle_k_entry or constructor ...'). Decide whether the negation means 'this function does not perform X' or 'the input has not undergone X'. If the true statement is a precondition on the input, rewrite it as the positive precondition ('pre-shuffled').
detection.question: Does the negated phrase state a precondition on the input or the absence of a step, and which one is true?

members.quote: would this read better if it said `These functions transfer pre-shuffled cacheblocks to HBM`?
members.note: Verified at the final head f0134b976b: h/libpos.hpp:276 reads 'These functions transfer pre-shuffled cacheblocks to HBM.' The same comment block's example says 'populate k_block via shuffle_k_entry', which is the fact Wade relied on. Phrased as a question ('would this read better'), not a suggestion block.

members.concern: A header comment tells the reader to see a file for_claude/heap-profile.log that exists only on the author's machine and is not in the change set; Wade points out nobody else can open it.

detection.trigger: An added comment, Note or doc line names a file path (contains '/' and an extension, or a directory such as for_claude/, tmp/, /home/, /var/tmp/) that is not under the repository or not in the PR's file list.
detection.procedure: Extract every path-like token from the diff's added comment lines; for each, run `git ls-files <path>` at HEAD and check the PR file list; report every path that resolves nowhere.
detection.question: Can a reader of the repository at HEAD open the file this comment points to?

members.quote: `for_claude/heap-profile.log` probably won't exist for anybody else but you ;p?
members.note: Check 9 covers machine-local paths and log names but only inside PR-body Status/Verification/Tests/Results sections; this hit is in a header comment, so the trigger as written does not fire. Author deleted the reference in commit e4c4f49452 ('Uncomment for fragmentation research.').

members.concern: Wade asks whether the parenthetical '(C2C egress excepted)' in the new Silver-language paragraph means 'accepted' or 'is the exception', because the elided clause reads two ways (C2C = chip-to-chip link; Silver = the proposed command language of the abstract machine).

detection.trigger: A prose hunk (doc, Note, or comment) adds a parenthetical or elided clause whose key word has a near-homophone or sibling word with the opposite sense (excepted/accepted, affect/effect) or whose subject and verb are omitted.
detection.procedure: For every added sentence in docs/ and comment hunks, expand each parenthetical or verb-less clause into two full sentences, one per plausible reading. If both expansions are grammatical and differ in meaning, ask the author which one is meant and propose the full-sentence form.
detection.question: Can a first-time reader expand this clause into exactly one full sentence?

members.quote: is this meant to say "C2C egress accepted"? Or perhaps "C2C egress is the exception"? I would imagine both are true.
members.note: Author replied that both readings were intended and rewrote the sentence in 3b1f9ae to 'C2C egress is the exception because its port mask can select links from both hemispheres'. Wade needed only the hunk; the ambiguity is in the added line itself.

members.concern: Comment wording: the member comment 'kv_shard_layers[l]: k/v HBM bases and alloc size' repeats the identifier; he suggests 'per-layer k/v HBM bases and alloc size'.

detection.trigger: A trailing comment on a declaration begins by restating the declared name (`name[i]: ...`, `name is ...`), especially after a rename made the name self-describing.
detection.procedure: For each added declaration with a trailing comment, check whether the comment's first token is the identifier; propose a reworded comment that states only what the name does not.
detection.question: Does the comment add information beyond the identifier, and does it start with the identifier?

members.quote: kv_shard_layers;  // per-layer k/v HBM bases and alloc size
members.note: Not applied at head (shard.hpp:37 still 'kv_shard_layers[l]: ...'). Follow-on from his own rename request 2982403509: once the name was descriptive, the comment's '[l]:' prefix became noise.

codex_bullets.bullet: Define the unit being counted and the classification granularity. A forward containing prefill and decode work cannot establish decode-only behavior unless that limitation is explicit.
codex_bullets.reason: One strong comment (4596) and two weaker naming checks (3490, 2980). The second sentence is PR 4596 specific; adopt the first sentence only.

codex_bullets.bullet: Use stable worker or device identity for cumulative rows. Distinguish a pool thread from its temporary role. Verify exported names, debug strings, and documentation against the actual index.
codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 4596, 2980). The third sentence (exported names vs actual index) has two independent hits.

codex_bullets.bullet: Label results with their tested revision and relevant configuration. Keep usable artifact references and outcomes. Remove obsolete arithmetic and local bookkeeping that do not help a reviewer assess the change.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4557, 4596, 2713; 5420005787 quoted twice). Claude checks 8 and 9 cover revision labels and unusable passages.

codex_bullets.bullet: Keep comments about lasting behavior and rationale. Remove review-round labels, story narration, stale questions, and debug residue. A large explanatory Note is useful only when the mechanism needs it.
codex_bullets.reason: Largest cluster in the corpus: at least 14 comments on debug residue, commented-out code, left-enabled debug macros, stale comments and review narration (also 4146959502, 2771711406, 2737935271, 2789808472, 2759903853, 3350412400, 3973917755, 3102601258, 2915191812). The positron-code-review skill covers narration but the Wade skill has nothing.
